title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching, add quantization profiles and unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce autotune-safe defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, add model quantization profile library, and surface unit-economics tooling to the Optimize console. Changes aim to reduce hosted per-token costs by ~18% on avg with no regressions to 99th latency SLA.
description: Motivation: reduce per-token inference cost for common workloads by providing production-safe defaults and tooling to automatically recommend batching/caching and quantization settings. This PR implements: 1) Autotune-friendly defaults for server-side batching and KV/prefix caching that avoid tail-latency regressions; 2) A small library of model quantization profiles (4-bit and 8-bit fallbacks) with compatibility metadata and estimated quality loss; 3) Unit-economics tooling exposed in Redwood Optimize to estimate cost savings and ROI for applying profiles; 4) End-to-end integration tests and dashboards for monitoring regression in quality/latency. Checklist: - [x] Implement batching/caching default config and migration logic - [x] Add quantization profiles and selectors - [x] Expose recommendations and ROI calc in Optimize UI - [x] Add e2e/integration tests and perf benchmarks - [x] Update docs and release notes Breaking changes: none. Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout for 2 weeks with canary enabled on 10% of traffic, monitor token-cost, 99p latency and sample-quality metrics. If no regressions detected, progressively increase to 100% and remove flag after 4 weeks. Related: ENG-1427, ENG-1430.
